coupled_design.content_idea: Repair is a small shared accomplishment made through contact: a neighbor braces a loose chair rail while another turns a screwdriver, and a second pair tensions a torn shirt while one stitches. Both tasks belong to one current encounter at the same bench, with faces, upper bodies, worn sleeves, hands and full recognizable repair objects in one continuous view.
coupled_design.whole_scene_execution: Use a slightly elevated elbow-height view close enough that the near two bodies crop at the lower edges and the upper two faces and bent shoulders remain legible. The chair occupies the left near edge; its back slats, seat, splayed legs and loose rail stay recognizable. At right, a shirt's collar and sleeves remain whole enough to identify clothing, while the tear and a small repair stitch are held between two neighbors. Give the left pair distinct hands: one stabilizes the same rail the other's driver tip actually meets. At right, one hand holds cloth on either side of the tear and another grips the needle, with thread visibly under modest tension. Shared directional light, continuous tabletop grain and consistent contact shadows join all four people into one place.
coupled_design.spatial_and_crop_decisions: Budget the paragraph's 730x174 guide area first. The upper faces and bent arms open a gently narrowing light interval that becomes the bench plane; the paragraph remains a flat typographic overlay within this active interval. Large bodies and objects continue around it to the image edges. The table edge is visible outside the paragraph, with a softened tonal transition through the opening above it. The lower action axis begins beyond the chair's outer leg. Let image contours and gestures determine this interval and keep the gestures recognizably substantial.
coupled_design.type_coupling: Use an open, relatively light display title as the invitation into the scene, a compact medium Latin register, then a regular proposition leading to a precise, medium-optical-body explanation. The title follows the space between bent heads; the paragraph begins just inside the working-light plane; the last learning phrase leads by adjacency to workshop identity. A descending left optical edge links workshop, date/time, venue and cost. Deadline, object invitation and URL finish as one adjoining run. Keep every baseline flat, natural word spaces intact, and the three body lines together even as the scene's plane shifts around them.
coupled_design.material_color_emotion: Single continuous documentary color photograph of the current shared repair encounter. Quiet daylight, deep indigo clothing, warm skin, visibly worn wood and cotton. Closely observed real human proportions, recognizable two repair contacts and coherent light. Every region belongs to this one photograph; no invented painted room, no stock collage strips. Retain crisp flat printed text in the light interval between bent working bodies. Diagram gray/clipart is only a scale/copy plan and does not prescribe imagery or final colors.
coupled_design.recognizable_visual_evidence: Four human figures with visible heads and arms, one large chair, one large shirt, two paired repair contacts, a screwdriver tip meeting the chair joint and a held needle/thread meeting the shirt tear. The meaningful image is the joint work itself.
